sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Undeclared or uninitialized variables cause compilation errors
Integer overflow wraps around silently: 2147483647 + 1 becomes -2147483648
Mixing Scanner methods like nextInt() and nextLine() can skip input unexpectedly
Off-by-one errors often occur when counting or iterating over ranges

questions.question: What is a common error when dividing two integers in Java?
options: Expecting a decimal result from integer division
questions.explanation: A common beginner mistake is expecting 5/2 to give 2.5. In Java, integer division truncates the decimal part, giving 2. Use double types or cast to get decimal results.

questions.question: Which of the following will cause a compilation error?
questions.explanation: Assigning a double literal (3.14) directly to an int variable causes a compilation error because it is a narrowing conversion that could lose data. You need an explicit cast: int z = (int) 3.14;
